title: Sharpening Tax in Post-Training
authors: Changdae Oh, Qi Zeng, Qi Qi, Andrey Zhmoginov, Deren Lei, Yun He, Hoang Phan, Hangoo Kang, Azalia Mirhoseini, Sharon Li
lab: Meta Superintelligence Labs, University of Wisconsin-Madison, NYU, Stanford University (the first author's work done at Meta)
date: 1 October 2026 (arXiv v1, the only version as of 19 October 2026)

code.title: changdaeoh/sharpening-tax
code.note: The metrics, the text harness, the PTGS controller, a CPU toy and the per-task success counts of all 42 cells (CC BY-NC 4.0, read at commit 789ae06c on 19 October 2026). The README calls it "minimal working examples ... not a reproduction package": no RL training code for the Table 2 runs, no rollout logs

takeaway: On three agentic benchmarks and 14 open base/post-trained pairs, post-training trades retry value for pass@1: the Sharpening Tax is positive in 36 of 42 cells, with tasks polarising toward always-solved or never-solved. The base model reaches more tasks at pass@128 in only 26 cells (clearly in 18, mostly larger models), with an authors' harness for the base side and post-trained models run without thinking at one shared temperature. Per-prompt tempered sampling (PTGS) is a promising but not yet demonstrated mitigation: five runs on two grid games, tax reductions within the noise.
takeaway_note: Scoped on 26 October 2026. The database Takeaway as fetched said base models with a light harness often beat their post-trained versions at pass@K in "most of 42 cases" and that PTGS pays a smaller tax and raises pass@1; the 19 October correction kept "because post-training pushes tasks" (the paper shows polarisation alongside the tax, an observational link, not a tested cause) and left out the decoding set-up the gap depends on. The Notion property needs the same edit.
verdict: Believe the measurement: the released per-task counts reproduce every Sharpening Tax, coverage and task-category number in the appendix tables, and the 36 of 42 positive taxes hold. Keep the two counts apart: the tax is positive in 36 of 42 cells, while the base model reaches more tasks at pass@128 in 26, clearly (the interval excludes zero) in 18, mostly for the larger models. Treat PTGS as promising, not shown: five runs per arm in two grid-world games on one 7B model, the tax reductions sit inside the run-to-run noise, and a plain fixed temperature of 0.5 paid a smaller tax than PTGS in both games.

headline.k: model-benchmark pairs where post-training lowers calibrated test-time scalability (TaxS(128) > 0); the replay of the released counts gives the same 42 values
headline.d: negative ones: small models on BFCL, where post-training fixes tool-call formatting

headline.k: gemma-4-31B on WebShop: the base model with a harness against its instruction-tuned version, which leads at pass@1 (23 against 40%) until k = 3
headline.d: base ahead at k = 128 in 26 of 42 cells, 18 with the interval clear of zero

headline.k: PPO on Sokoban without and with PTGS, while pass@1 rose 46.5 to 61.1 and pass@128 55.0 to 69.7 (five runs each)
headline.d: the tax drop is under one standard error; a fixed T = 0.5 reached 0.073
